entry.name: mc.mixdown~
entry.digest: Mix and pan a multichannel signal
entry.description: The mc.mixdown~ object mixes channels in a multichannel signal connected to its left inlet to a multichannel output. mc.mixdown~ can use a signal connected to its right inlet to pan the channels of its left (mix) input signal.

arguments.name: output-channel-count
arguments.description: An optional argument sets the number of channels in the multichannel output signal (default 2).

attributes.name: activechans
attributes.digest: Active Channels
attributes.description: Setting theattribute reduces the number of channels that will be used for mixing. Extra channels will be set to zero. Use ofprovides a way to set different output mix channel counts without repatching. For example, you could switch your patch from multichannel to stereo output by using anobject with an argument of 5, then settingto 2 at runtime.

attributes.name: linearpanmode
attributes.digest: Linear Pan Mode
attributes.description: When enabled,applies a linear pan scaling factor to all input channels. This scaling factor is set by theattribute (default 1). Whenis disabled (the default),applies a constant power pan scale factor (square root of 2 over 2).

attributes.name: linearpanscalefactor
attributes.digest: Linear Pan Scale Factor
attributes.description: Sets the panning scale factor to apply to all input channels whenis enabled (default 1).

attributes.name: pancontrolmode
attributes.digest: Pan Control Mode
attributes.description: Thedetermines howinterprets values in its pan input signal. In all pan control modes, values outside the specified range are wrapped around to be within the range.

choices.label: Whenis 0 (default),interprets pan values in a circular map with 0.5 defined as the "front" position between the two middle channels (if there are an even number of output channels) or the center channel (if there are an odd number of output channels). For stereo output, panning all the way to the left (channel 1) is at 0.25 and panning all the way to the right (channel 2) is at 0.75. For higher output channel counts, exact pan for a specific channel can be calculated by dividing 1 by twice the number of output channels and then using odd numbers for the value of the numerator. For example, for 4 channels, the exact pan for channel 1 is at 1/8 (0.125), channel 2 is at 3/8 (0.375), channel 3 is at 5/8 (0.625), and channel 4 is at 7/8 (0.875). (If all this math seems daunting, look at the othersettings below.)

Whenis 1, all channels are arranged in a line with panning to the first channel at 0 and the last channel at 1. This prevents any panning between the first and last channel in a case where the number of outputs are larger than 2. However, for the 2-channel output case where this is not an issue, it is often more convenient to produce a signal where 0 represents channel 1 and 1 represents channel 2.

Whenis 2, all channels are arranged in a line with panning to the first channel at 1 and the last channel when the the pan value is equal to the output channel count. This prevents any panning between the first and last channel in a case where the number of outputs are larger than 2.

Whenis 3,interprets pan values in a circular map where panning only to each output channel is represented by a whole number. Values between 0 and 1 represent a pan position between the first and last output channels.

attributes.name: usebusymap
attributes.digest: Use Allocator Busy Map
attributes.description: Whenis enabled,will not mix non-busy channels in its mix input. This can increase efficiency and avoid unpleasant noise when mixing channels that are not set to zero. Note that the wayuses the busy map is somewhat different from the way the MC wrapper uses it, but the two systems are designed to work together.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: In left inlet: a multichannel signal to mixIn right inlet: a single- or multichannel signal with pan informationWithout a signal connected to the right inlet,alternates input channels to output channels (output channel 1 contains inputs 1, 3, 5, ... and output channel 2 contains input 2, 4, 6...). With a signal connected to the right inlet,performs N-way panning. The pan behavior is determined by the,, andattributes.

inlets.description: Pan position for corresponding mix input channel

outlets.description: outputs a multichannel signal mixed from the channels in its left input. The number of channels in the output is set by the argument to theobject, and the number of channels in the mix is determined by the current value of theattribute. Extra channels are zero.
